rationale: The literature presents conflicting evidence regarding the frequency of microcephaly and seizures in LRRC7-related intellectual developmental disorder (OMIM #621415). In the largest systematic cohort study to date (Willim et al., 2024; n=33), core cardinal features were intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, aggression, and hyperphagia, while seizures were present in only a minority (6/33; 18.2%), supporting the premise that seizures and specific cranial dysmorphic features are secondary rather than cardinal features. However, Khan et al. (2026) report that microcephaly is observed in approximately one-third (~33%) of reported LRRC7 cases, directly contradicting the hypothesis that microcephaly represents an isolated, private phenotypic expansion occurring in <10% of cases. In addition, early infancy seizures have been documented across multiple distinct probands (e.g., Popp et al., 2017 and Khan et al., 2026), refuting the notion that infancy-onset seizures are entirely private to the p.Pro887Leu variant.

evidence.text: A proband with a de novo heterozygous missense variant in LRRC7 [c.2660C>T; p.(Pro887Leu)] presented with global developmental delay, tonic seizures, failure to thrive, mild microcephaly, intellectual disability, and hypotonia. Notably, the study notes that microcephaly is present in roughly one-third of reported cases.

conflicts: Khan et al. (2026) report that microcephaly occurs in approximately one-third (~33%) of reported LRRC7 cases, conflicting with the hypothesis that structural cranial abnormalities are infrequent/private (<10%).

Early infancy-onset seizures are reported in multiple unrelated probands across different variant classes (including a de novo loss-of-function variant described by Popp et al., 2017 and a missense variant by Khan et al., 2026), refuting the claim that infantile seizures are an isolated, private feature restricted to specific linker-region missense variants.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true frequency of standardized occipitofrontal circumference (OFC) <-2 SD across all published LRRC7 variant carriers when aggregating clinical measurement data?
new_directions.rationale: Statements claiming microcephaly occurs in ~33% of cases must be systematically verified against individual-level anthropometric Z-scores across all cohort papers to resolve the conflict with larger series reporting absence of recurrent dysmorphic cranial signs.

new_directions.question_text: Do variants mapping to the LRRC7 linker region alter protein-protein interactions differently than LRR or PDZ domain variants in a way that correlates with seizure severity?
new_directions.rationale: Willim et al. (2024) demonstrated domain-specific functional consequences (e.g., PDZ domain altering synaptic targeting; LRR domain disrupting PP1 binding). Assessing linker-region variants like p.Pro887Leu in similar assays could establish if epileptogenic mechanisms are variant-specific.
